summary: Build a local-first CV research crawler (FastAPI + React) that ingests papers and GitHub repos from 4 source types on a schedule, exposes a web panel for browsing/filtering/tagging, and generates daily/weekly Markdown reports. V1 prioritizes arxiv + GitHub crawling, paper/repo browsing with filters, a tag system, and scheduled report generation -- all deployable as a single Docker Compose stack with SQLite for local use or PostgreSQL for server deployment.
key_decisions: Modular monolith over microservices: the system is single-user, local-first; a monolith with a plugin-based crawler registry gives us extensibility without distributed-system complexity.

Unified BaseCrawler interface (fetch -> normalize -> upsert): every data source implements the same three-method contract, so adding a new source is a single new file plus registry registration -- no core changes.

SQLAlchemy ORM with SQLite default and PostgreSQL option: zero-setup local development via SQLite WAL mode; one connection-string change for server deployment. Alembic handles migrations in both environments.

APScheduler for cron-style scheduling over Celery/RQ: lightweight, in-process, no external broker required for V1. Sufficient for single-instance deployments. Can swap to Celery later if horizontal scaling is needed.
React + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind over Next.js or Create React App: the frontend is a pure SPA with no SSR requirement; Vite gives fast dev iteration and small production bundles.
Jinja2 for Markdown report rendering over a headless CMS or database-stored templates: templates are version-controlled text files in the repo, easy to edit, and map naturally to Markdown output.
UUID primary keys over auto-increment integers: safer for potential future distributed scenarios, avoids ID collision if data is ever merged across instances.
Explicit CrawlLog table from day one: provides an audit trail for every crawl run, making debugging and monitoring straightforward without external infrastructure.
open_questions: Should we support API tokens for arxiv (they have a polite-use policy but no official rate limit) -- what is the minimum crawl interval that keeps us within their guidelines?
Papers With Code has no official API; scraping HTML is fragile. Should V1 defer PWC or use an unofficial third-party dataset snapshot?
Do we need full-text search beyond SQL LIKE? SQLite FTS5 vs. bringing in Elasticsearch/Meilisearch later?
Conference proceedings from dblp/OpenReview: should the system attempt to match them against their arxiv preprint versions (many papers appear on both), or store them as separate entries?
Report delivery: filesystem-only is sufficient for V1, but should the Report model include a `delivery_status` field now to accommodate email/Slack/webhook delivery later without a migration?
Tag color palette: enforce a fixed set of 12-16 colors or allow free-form hex input?
Data retention: should we auto-prune papers older than N months from the browse view, or keep everything and rely on filters?
Is the 2-hour GitHub crawl frequency too aggressive for unauthenticated / basic-token access? Should it be configurable per environment variable?
